clue.text: Disturbance with nasty blow in region of US

parts.note: a dust, as in 'kick up a dust', is a commotion or row

indicators.note: nasty suggests the word blow has been roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A violent gust of wind causes trouble somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges BLOW into BOWL. The Dust Bowl was the drought-stricken prairie region of the 1930s USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dust Bowl was the area of the American Great Plains ruined by drought and storms in the 1930s.

clue.text: One line in code cracked — easily managed

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is set inside the scrambled code
a code that is cracked is broken open, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A codebreaker reports that one line yielded easily once the cipher was cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' is the anagram signal for the code (giving DOCE), and 'in' sets the one and the line inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A docile animal or person is tame and compliant, readily handled.

clue.text: Tack with the least scrap of sails

definitions.meaning: to tack is to fasten with loose temporary sewing
sailors speak of carrying every ... of canvas, a ... being the smallest piece of sail

explanation.surface: A sailor changes course while carrying almost no canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacking is loose sewing done in single passes of the needle, and in sailing slang a single scrap of sailcloth is called a stitch, as in 'every stitch of canvas'.

clue.text: Push forward with Bishop, one in support

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: in places the single letter within the word for support

parts.note: a rest is a prop or support
a means one

explanation.surface: A chess player pushes a bishop forward, with another piece backing it up.
explanation.walkthrough: To breast something is to push forward against it, as a runner breasts the tape.
explanation.definitionFit: To breast a wave or the tape is to advance against it with the chest, pressing onward.

clue.text: Eastern rolling shore covered by a little wave

indicators.note: in a down clue, being covered by something means sitting beneath it, so that piece comes first

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'

indicators.note: rolling suggests the letters of shore tumbling into another order

explanation.surface: Waves roll onto an eastern shore, washed over by a small breaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling' is the anagram signal, making a horse of the shore; 'covered by' means placed below in a down entry, so the little bit comes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: White horses are the foam-crested breakers seen on a choppy sea.

clue.text: Drink knocked back at English feast

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so the drink's word is read from its end

parts.note: lager is a pale beer

explanation.surface: Someone downs a beer at a hearty English banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses LAGER to REGAL. Feast is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale guests is to entertain them lavishly with food and drink.

clue.text: Six geese flying wildly — what's the explanation?

indicators.note: geese flying wildly break formation, so the letters of the two words are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone sees six geese careering about and asks why.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is critical interpretation, especially of scripture.

clue.text: Driving energy from circuit, one working

parts.note: an ambit is a circuit or boundary
one is the Roman numeral I
on means functioning, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Motor-racing talk: the energy powering a car around the track while the engine runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambition is the strong desire and drive that pushes someone toward success.

clue.text: Monocle to ogle German girl

parts.note: to eye someone is to look at them, here leeringly
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A man screws in his monocle to leer at a German girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single lens held in front of one eye.

clue.text: Canons caught ceremony broadcast to the West

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means running right to left, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Church canons are seen at a service televised to Western audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the West' turns AIR into RIA. Canons here are rules or standards, not clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Canons are accepted rules or standards for judging, so they are the benchmarks.

clue.text: Ineffective complaint rejected by the French

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for complaint is read backwards

parts.note: a beef is a grievance
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A grievance is brushed aside by the French as having no force.
explanation.definitionFit: Something feeble is weak and lacking force.

clue.text: Secure a degree in March, sort of?

parts.note: to lock something is to secure it
a step is a degree or stage on a scale

explanation.surface: Someone seeks to gain a qualification in the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: March is a verb here, not the month: lockstep is a way of marching very close together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockstep is marching in a tight file where each person's feet follow those in front exactly.

clue.text: Pulse is fast, one-fifty

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
one is the Roman numeral I
fifty is the Roman numeral L

explanation.surface: A heart rate check finds a pulse running at one hundred and fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulse here is the edible seed, not the heartbeat; 'fast' is the noun, a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible legume seeds, and a lentil is one kind.

clue.text: Solitary ornate antique gets smuggled in

indicators.note: in shows one piece being placed inside the rearranged antique
ornate suggests the letters of antique are elaborately reworked

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so ran is the past tense

explanation.surface: A lone, elaborate antique is brought into the country illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornate' rearranges the antique (to QUATINE) and 'in' puts the smuggled run inside it. Solitary is a noun, as in solitary confinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary confinement and quarantine both mean being kept isolated from other people.

clue.text: Bulky, see — nothing very light

parts.note: v. abbreviates Latin vide, meaning see, in references
O is zero, nothing
luminous means giving out bright light

explanation.surface: Look: something big yet weighing almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'v.' of footnotes stands for vide, Latin for 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something voluminous is large and roomy, taking up a lot of space.

clue.text: Occasional random cop raids

indicators.note: random suggests the letters of the phrase are thrown into a haphazard order

explanation.surface: The police make unplanned raids now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means happening irregularly or now and again.

clue.text: Odd piece pinched by present felon

indicators.note: pinched by means held tightly within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to offer is to present
an end is a leftover piece, as in odds and ends

explanation.surface: A criminal is caught stealing an odd item from a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' sounds like theft, but here it means gripped tight, so the odd piece is held inside the present.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is a criminal, someone who has committed an offence.

clue.text: It's a blow having stimulant reduced

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
cut means reduced, as with prices

explanation.surface: Losing one's supply of pep pills is disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a blow' reads as 'that's a pity' but names the punch.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a punch thrown upward at the chin.

clue.text: Swell old line in bakery produce

parts.note: to puff up is to swell
past means former or old
RY abbreviates railway, a rail line

explanation.surface: Dough rises nicely in a traditional baker's goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Puff pastry is a light flaky dough made in bakeries.

clue.text: Discharge from bench

definitions.meaning: to ... a debt is to pay it off

explanation.surface: Someone is released from the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying off a bill is discharging it, and an old-fashioned high-backed wooden seat for several people is also called by this name.

clue.text: Devil's responsible for Testament's original sin

indicators.note: original means the first, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: an error is a wrong or transgression

explanation.surface: The Devil is blamed for original sin in the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original sin' sounds like theology, but 'original' picks T from Testament. A Devil here is a naughty child, a little terror.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child is called a little devil or a little terror.

clue.text: Hard time inside makes one stoical

indicators.note: inside places one letter within the word for hard

parts.note: solid means hard and firm

explanation.surface: A tough prison sentence makes a person impassive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard time' looks like a prison sentence, but splits into SOLID and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is calm and unemotional, impassive.

clue.text: Rock'n'roller, or another kind of dancer?

definitions.meaning: someone who rocks and rolls, staggering about
one who dances a Scottish reel

explanation.surface: A rock'n'roll fan wonders about other dance styles.
explanation.definitionFit: One who staggers about is a reeler, and so is a performer of the Scottish reel dance.

clue.text: Benefit of endless winter break

indicators.note: endless means without its ends, so the first and last letters of winter are dropped

parts.note: a rest is a break

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys an unending winter holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest is advantage or profit, something in one's favour.

clue.text: Infer editor's cut wartime leader

indicators.note: cut means sliced into, so one piece is set inside the leader's title

parts.note: Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, Italy's wartime dictator
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone works out that a newspaper editor removed a dictator from the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'editor's cut' looks like a film's edited version; instead the editor cuts into Mussolini's title, Il Duce.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reach a conclusion by reasoning.

clue.text: Like the seaside? That sounds unimaginative

indicators.note: sounds tells us the word for unimaginative is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: literal means matter-of-fact and lacking imagination

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a seaside description as dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Littoral means relating to the shore, the coastal zone.

clue.text: Clergyman's jalopy parked outside University

indicators.note: parked outside means the vehicle's word sits around another letter

parts.note: a crate is a decrepit old car

explanation.surface: A vicar's battered car is left outside the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant to a parish priest.

clue.text: Committed (proved wrong) by judge

parts.note: a referee, ref for short, judges a match
erred means made a mistake

explanation.surface: A referee was mistaken and then sent off a player.
explanation.definitionFit: A case committed for trial has been sent on or passed to a higher court.
